control_provenance.description: Check that a container image is signed by the identity this descriptor expects.

signers.description: Who is expected to have signed what. A signer names itself, the images it covers, and the identity to check against.

github.description: A GitHub Actions signer written as its parts. Expands to the keyless issuer and identity, which draugr validate prints.

ref.description: The git ref the workflow ran at, e.g. "refs/heads/main" or "refs/tags/v3".

repository.description: The repository whose workflow signs, as owner/name. A job calling a reusable workflow is signed as that workflow's repository, not as the caller's.

images.description: Image references this signer covers, where * matches any run of characters, e.g. ["ghcr.io/acme/*"]. An image no signer covers is observed rather than checked.

keyless.description: A Sigstore keyless signature, identified by who issued the token and which workload it named.

identity.description: The exact signing identity, e.g. "https://github.com/acme/ci/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/tags/v3". A job calling a reusable workflow is signed as that workflow, not as the caller. Run the control with no signers declared and read it back from --format sarif.

identityRegexp.description: A Go regular expression the identity must match, for a signer covering several workflows. A pattern loose enough to match anything accepts a signature from anybody.

issuer.description: The OIDC issuer, e.g. "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com" for GitHub Actions or your GitLab instance URL for GitLab CI.

name.description: What to call this signer, e.g. "our-ci". Referenced by an image's signedBy.

x509.description: A Notary Project signature, identified by the certificate it carries and the roots that certificate must chain to. What Azure Pipelines produces with a key in Azure Key Vault, and what an in-house PKI produces.

subject.description: The certificate subject to require, as a comma-separated distinguished name, e.g. "C=US, ST=WA, O=Acme, CN=Acme Release Signing". Run notation inspect on the image to read the exact string.

trustStore.description: Path to a PEM file of root certificates the signing certificate must chain to, relative to where Draugr runs.

trustRoot.description: Path to a Sigstore trusted-root JSON file, for a runner that cannot reach the transparency log. Without one, a runner with no egress reports an error rather than a pass.

anyOf.description: Report the identity found and expect nothing. Most of what a project runs is published by somebody else, so this is where a policy starts rather than where it ends.
Report an image no signer covers as a warning, without failing the gate on it.
Require every image to be covered by a signer. The end state, once the inventory has been worked through.

unmatched.description: What an image no signer covers is worth. Defaults to observe.

tags.description: Go build tags to compile with, e.g. ["integration"]. Code behind a tag gosec does not build is code it does not analyze.

filePatterns.description: More files for an analyzer to read, each analyzer:regex, e.g. ["pip:requirements-.*\\.txt"]. Trivy's pip analyzer reads only requirements.txt.

includeDevDeps.description: Report development dependencies too. Trivy leaves them out by default. Applies to npm, Yarn and Gradle.

control_secrets.description: Find passwords and keys committed by accident, history included.

config.description: Path to a Gitleaks TOML rules file, relative to where Draugr runs. Use it for a ruleset shared across repositories; a .gitleaks.toml committed in the scanned repository is already picked up without this.

enabled.description: Run this scanner. It is a default for this control, so it runs unless set to false.

history.description: Also scan the repository's commit history, in addition to the working tree. Off by default: it needs a full clone rather than a shallow one, so it is slower on a large repository. A secret committed and later removed is still fetchable by anyone who can clone, so it is still compromised, this is what finds it. History findings are marked as such, because they name the path the secret had when it was introduced, and are kept only when that path would be checked out by this component's paths and ignore. A secret still in the tree at the same path is reported once, as the tree finding.

requestsPerMinute.description: Override the assumed API allowance. Defaults to the public tier's 4. Raise it only to what your key actually permits, exceeding VirusTotal's limit risks losing access, and their stated penalty for terms violations is a permanent ban.

control_tls.description: Check the certificates and encryption a component's running endpoints offer visitors.

enabled.description: Run this scanner. It is a default for this control, so it runs unless set to false.

expiryErrorDays.description: Report an error when the certificate expires within this many days. Defaults to 14.

expiryWarnDays.description: Report a warning when the certificate expires within this many days. Defaults to 30. Lower it for endpoints with automated renewal so the gate only fires when renewal has failed.

enabled.description: Whether this control runs. An entry with no `enabled` key counts as enabled; an absent entry means disabled.

controllers.description: Security controls, keyed by name. A control runs only when enabled here (or on a component). Each scanner is configured under its own key inside the control.

description: The draugr.config.yaml file: settings for the machine or organization running a scan, layered underneath every descriptor it scans. See https://draugr.dev/docs/latest/reference/cli/#draugr-config

cache.description: Where scan results are reused between runs, and for how long.

dir.description: The directory results are cached in. Unset leaves caching off. Overridden by `--cache-dir`.

readOnly.description: Serve cached results without writing new ones. A project file's `false` does not override a `true` set in `~/.draugr/config.yaml`. Overridden by `--cache-read-only`.

requireDigest.description: Refuse to cache an image named only by a tag, which can be rebuilt under the same name. A project file's `false` does not override a `true` set in `~/.draugr/config.yaml`. Overridden by `--cache-require-digest`.

ttl.description: How long a cached result stays usable, as a duration such as `24h`. `0s` means no expiry; unset keeps the built-in default. Overridden by `--cache-ttl`.

controllers.description: Deprecated: write `controls`. Read as `controls`; `controls` wins where both set a key.

controls.description: Default settings for each control, merged underneath a descriptor's `config.controls`, so a project overrides only the keys it names. The same shape as `config.controls` in a Saga.

log.description: What Draugr logs, and in which format.

format.description: How log records are written. Overridden by `--log-format`.

level.description: The least severe level logged. Overridden by `--log-level`.

offline.description: Make no network calls: optional fetches are skipped, and commands that exist to download refuse. A more specific file's `false` does not turn it off. Overridden by `--offline` and `$DRAUGR_OFFLINE`.

output.description: How a console report is rendered. A flag on the command line overrides each setting.

evidence.description: Also print what stands behind the verdict: tool provenance, what each control measured against, the scanned revision, and what the run cost. Overridden by `--evidence`.

offerInstall.description: Whether `draugr scan` on a terminal offers to install the scanners it is missing. Unset means it offers.

tips.description: Whether a console scan prints its contextual tips and its progress line. Unset means it prints them. Overridden by `--no-tips` and `$DRAUGR_NO_TIPS`.

top.description: How many rows a console report lists. `0` keeps the command's own default, a cap for `scan` and every row for `diff`. Overridden by `--top`.

anyOf.description: A row per finding, with what argued with its band underneath.
A row per thing to do, each saying how many findings it clears.

view.description: What a console report shows. Overridden by `--view`.

publish.description: Defaults for where a run is delivered.

apiUrl.description: Where the `draugr-api` publisher posts when `$DRAUGR_API_URL` is unset. In a project's draugr.config.yaml it is used only on the origin of `publish.apiUrl` in `~/.draugr/config.yaml`, or one `$DRAUGR_API_ORIGINS` lists. Never holds a token.

scan.description: How a scan runs on this machine.

jobs.description: How many scan jobs run at once. `0` means one per CPU. Overridden by `--jobs`.

tools.description: The version of each external tool `draugr tools install` provisions, keyed by tool name.
